# Didache Chapter 5 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Codex Hierosolymitanus (H), Didache 5

---

## Chapter 5

**1** The way of death is this: above all it is evil and full of curse — murderers, adulterers, the lustful, the sexually immoral, thieves, idolaters, practitioners of magic, sorcerers, robbers, false witnesses, hypocrites, the deceitful, the crafty, the arrogant, the malicious, the self-willed, the greedy, the foul-mouthed, the jealous, the insolent, the proud, the boastful;

**2** persecutors of the good, haters of truth, lovers of falsehood — who do not acknowledge the reward of righteousness, who do not hold to what is good or to righteous judgment, who lie awake planning evil rather than good — from whom gentleness and patience are utterly absent — lovers of vain things, chasers of reward, who have no compassion for the poor, who do not exert themselves for the burdened, who do not acknowledge their Maker, murderers of children, corruptors of what God has formed, who turn away from one who is in need, who crush the afflicted, advocates of the wealthy, lawless judges of the poor — sinners in every way. Children, may you be delivered from all of these.

---

### Council Notes

**On structure:** All three agents rightly preserve the overwhelming, cumulative structure. PNEUMA's dramatic expansion is vivid but departs too far from the text's own measured list. SOPHIA follows LOGOS's more restrained structure while incorporating its best word choices.

**On v.2 (φθορεῖς πλάσματος θεοῦ):** All agents agree this is a key phrase. EMET's "destroyers of the image of God" is slightly off — πλάσμα is "what is formed/molded" (from Gen 2:7, where God forms humanity), not εἰκών (image). LOGOS's "corruptors of what God has formed" is more precise. SOPHIA adopts this rendering.

**On v.2 ("murderers of children"):** EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA all preserve this stark phrase. It likely encompasses abortion, infanticide, and child abandonment — the full range of ways in which children were killed in the ancient world. No softening is appropriate.

**On v.2 ("advocates of the wealthy / lawless judges"):** The closing sequence of the vice list is explicitly socioeconomic. PNEUMA helpfully emphasizes this; SOPHIA retains the formal structure while keeping the words "advocates of the wealthy" and "lawless judges of the poor" which are precise translations of the Greek.

**On closing address ("Children"):** All agents agree. The warm direct address τέκνα (Children) closes the Two Ways section with pastoral urgency — the same address used throughout chs. 3–4. This is not a legal verdict but a teacher's plea.
